prompt: Stage 3-5, level 7, 52 gold, 71 HP, a stable mid-lobby board that has gone win, loss, win. Mama Beak is 2-star with Rageblade and Infinity Edge, Sentinel holds the tank items. Hecarim is 1-star on the board with a second copy on the bench. The shop shows a Kayle (your third, 2 gold) and a Malphite (4 gold). Level 8 and the rolldown are planned for 4-2. What do you buy this round?

options.label: Buy the Kayle for the 2-star and nothing else: you stay at exactly 50
Buy the Kayle and roll twice for the third Hecarim: a 2-star frontline for 6 gold
Buy the Kayle and the Malphite: a 4-cost body is a bigger upgrade than a 2-star Hecarim
Buy nothing; 52 is above the floor and every gold counts at 4-2

explanation:
There is a line between spending the surplus and breaking the floor, and this round sits on it. The Kayle is a free 2-star: she is on your board, she costs 2, and 52 minus 2 is 50, so you lose nothing at 3-6. Buying nothing leaves 2 gold above the cap earning nothing and a 1-star on the board for no reason.

Rolling twice for Hecarim is the marginal upgrade the floor exists to refuse. At level 7 a slot is a 3-cost 43% of the time and there are fourteen 3-costs, so a specific one is in roughly 13% of shops; two shops find him about one time in four. The price is 4 gold of rolls plus 1 interest at 3-6, for an itemless 2-star 3-cost that a 4-cost tank replaces at 4-2. Malphite is worse: a single 4-cost you are not building around, bought at 3-5, drops you to 46 for a unit that wins no fight Sentinel was losing. Reach 4-2 at 60-plus and level 8; that is where the upgrades are.
principle: Spend the surplus above 50 freely; spend the gold below it only for a fight you are losing.
commonMistake: Treating 'I am winning anyway' as a licence to roll for small frontline upgrades three rounds before the planned rolldown.
hint: Price each purchase against 50: which ones leave you on the floor and which take you under it, and what each buys for the 4-2 fight.
